reader.requirement: At --std 85, a START with the KEY phrase on an indexed file must compare the file's keys of reference against the content of data-name-1 (the record key itself, or an alphanumeric item of any record of the file that begins at a record key's leftmost position and is no longer than it, SR4), the longer operand truncated to the shorter (GR4), under each of the 1985 operators (=, >, NOT <, >=, in words or symbols), and not against the RECORD KEY item (that is GR12, without the KEY phrase). The witnesses cover the no-KEY form and the refusal of the 2002 reverse operators, not GR11's own comparison.

edition-consulted.switches: EditionInfo.SubscriptedClauseOperands is Year == 2002: only 2002 admits a subscripted data-name-1; 85 refuses it with COBOL0862, as 2023 does
the reverse operators LESS, NOT GREATER, LESS OR EQUAL (COBOL0900 below 2002)

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the comparison itself; 1985 lacks the reverse operators, WITH LENGTH and FIRST/LAST, which are refused at 85, and 2002 alone admits a subscripted data-name-1
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the comparison against a shorter data-name-1 at a key's leftmost position, an item of another record description, the alternate key with a prime key holding other content, and each forward operator are not exercised

reader.notes: EmitStart sends the whole record area and the length of data-name-1, and the connector slices the key of reference out of the area. At 1985 that is the same thing as comparing data-name-1's content, because SR4 confines data-name-1 to the leftmost positions of a key within a record of the file, which all share the one record area. Every forward operator and both truncation directions behaved as GR4 and GR11 say.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:IX.4.7 whole (SR1-4, GR1-12) and the 1985 appendix item that the indexed file's collating sequence is the native one. Probes at --std 85 under refute-1985-01/: r4-coll (class c, PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS REV reversing Z..A, START KEY > K2 = 'B' through a 1-character item of a second record): 'AFTER START K2 > B: Z1zzzz' and sequential order A1/B1/Z1, so the comparison uses data-name-1 under the native sequence, not the program sequence; r4-qual (SR2 qualified data-name-1, two records each with HH and KK): Q1 KEY NOT LESS THAN HH OF R2 'MN' over the alternate key gives 0003MNN333; Q2 KEY > HH OF R3 'K' (1 of 3 positions) gives 0001MMM111; Q3 KEY >= KK OF R3 '0003' gives 0003; class e: Q0 START on a file open OUTPUT 'DECL 47 / Q0 AFTER 47' (INVALID KEY not taken, GR1), Q4 START after a failed OPEN (35) 'DECL 00 47 / Q4 AFTER 47'. Each result matches GR4 with GR11's data-name-1. The reader's slice-the-record-area design is equivalent at 1985 because SR4 and the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY rules put every data-name-1 in the file's one record area at a unique key's leftmost position. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.7.4 GR11; OK §1985:IX.4.7.4 GR4; OK §1985:IX.4.7.4 GR1; OK §1985:IX.4.7.3 SR2.
